assessments.reasoning: The cover and dated preface corroborate the initial Alto system context. The reproduced November 2 addendum identifies the object of the Version 1.0 manual’s intent as the expected Mesa language. The anticipated first-quarter compiler transfer supplies the time and distribution boundary. The text does not say the manual was intended to describe the compiler itself. The exact compound revision therefore fails direct support even though its Alto context and then-current language differences are supported.

challenge.method: Reacquire the same registered CHM PDF and check its exact digest. Read physical PDF pages 1, 2, 67 and 71. Test whether the grammatical object of the statement of intent is the language or the compiler itself, comparing the intended manual scope with the initial system context and the addendum’s grammar control.
challenge.results: Page 67 makes the expected Mesa language the subject matter of the manual and the transfer of its compiler the anticipated boundary. Page 71 separately supplies an addendum grammar. These passages oppose the exact compiler-description wording. Pages 1 and 2 confirm the context of the initial Alto programming system. The planned transfer date does not establish its actual occurrence.

limitations: This review applies to the December 1976 preliminary collection and its reproduced November 2 addendum, at the exact registered PDF revision.
The archival copy carries a historical internal-use notice. Only scope, source coordinates, and capture digests are shared.
No actual transfer, conformity, compiler implementation property, or cross-version compatibility is established by the printed statement of intent.
